source.title: cMoLLM at Scale: Horizontal Scaling Laws for Mixture-of-LLMs
source.authors: Xin Yang; Ye-Min Wang; Ming-Dao Liu; Le-Tian Li; Shuai Cao; Zhengxiao He; Ryan Dong

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some layout is flattened, and the conclusion refers to extended results in “??”, but the reported tables and sections relevant here are readable.
record.tranche_reason: It reports scaling measurements for a new pipeline-level mixture architecture, cMoLLM, rather than reproducing the original studies’ scaling-law fits.
record.gate_note: The study reports validation loss across three parameter scales and downstream scores across those scales. It does not fit power laws or report exponents. Its stream-count sweep in Table 2 varies a different capacity dimension, not parameters, tokens, or compute; it is not included as a row for the listed versions. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: In a new architecture (cMoLLM) and the dense GPT-2 baseline on FineWeb, it reports validation loss and downstream scores at three parameter sizes, 85M, 350M and 760M. This bears weakly on V1 and V6: it shows the direction of the trend but fits no power law and spans less than one order of magnitude.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that cMoLLM beats the dense baseline at every scale on loss, PPL, GLUE and SQuAD, and that it scales favorably with stream count and parameter count. They call the size trend 'consistent with standard scaling' without fitting a law. They also claim gains over ParaScale and AltUp, but report no numbers for those baselines.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and evaluates a new convolutionally gated mixture architecture; it does not use the original studies’ scaling-law fitting procedure. The code is stated to be planned for release upon acceptance.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with stream count and gating variant (Table 2); the authors also state that the load-balancing coefficient α has the largest hyperparameter impact (Section D).

fits_no_version.finding: Horizontal scaling in stream count: at fixed 85M size, loss and PPL improve as N goes from 1 to 4–8, with plateaus or mild overstreaming for some gating variants (Table 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss improves with the number of mixture streams at fixed model size, up to a saturation range.

record.code_released: not stated; the authors say the codebase will be made public upon acceptance
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The parameter-scaling results cover only three model sizes, from 85M to 760M. No power-law fitting, exponents, token-count or compute sweep, or compute-optimal allocation analysis is reported. The paper notes that validation at 7B+ parameters is needed.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports additional validation loss, perplexity, GLUE, and SQuAD v2 results by stream count and gating variant. Those vary stream count rather than parameter count, tokens, or compute, so they do not test the listed versions’ scaling quantities and were not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Power-law form, exponents, several orders of magnitude, and token or compute axes. Training tokens per run are not stated.
Quantitative predictability of downstream scores from scale or loss; only a monotone increase across three sizes is shown.
Not tested. Table 4 configurations change depth and width together with size.

missing.what: Training tokens or compute per model size. Without them it cannot be judged whether data was a bottleneck for the size sweep.
Validation loss vs training steps, which the Figure 3 caption mentions but the text gives no values for.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 limits_scope label was dropped: narrow range and no fit are untested parts, not qualifying results. Reported parameter counts look inconsistent with the configurations (12 layers, 768 hidden is usually about 124M). The conclusion cites unresolved '??' extended results. The ParaScale and AltUp comparisons have no reported numbers. Treat these results with caution.

versions.untested_parts: It measures validation loss at three parameter scales, but does not fit or test a power-law form, report exponents, cover several orders of magnitude, or vary training tokens or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict the losses of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep over parameter and token counts, or compute-optimal split, is reported.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Experiments concern FineWeb language-model pretraining; other modalities and training regimes are not tested.
It reports GLUE and SQuAD v2 scores across model sizes, but does not test a quantitative predictive relationship between downstream performance and pretraining loss.
The study reports some hyperparameter sensitivity but does not compare fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices, nor test bends away from a power law.
